question: This is a topographic map. The contour interval is 20 meters, index contours (heavy lines) are every 100 meters, and elevations are in meters. A fire lookout stands at the magenta square T. Four hikers are at the magenta points A, B, C and D. A hiker is hidden when the ground somewhere between rises above the straight sight line from T to that hiker. Ignore trees, eye height and the curvature of the Earth. Which hikers can the lookout see? Answer with their letters separated by commas, for example A, C.
references: USGS 7.5-minute topographic quadrangle maps (1:24 000, brown contours, bold index contours)
USGS Topographic Map Symbols booklet (contours, spot elevations, trails, streams)

question: This is a topographic map. The contour interval is 20 meters, index contours (heavy lines) are every 100 meters, and elevations are in meters. A hiker walks the Ridge Trail (dashed black line) from the magenta square S to the magenta square E. Estimate the walking time with Naismith's rule: 1 hour for every 4 km of map distance, plus 1 hour for every 300 m of ascent. Add up every uphill stretch along the way; downhill stretches add no time and do not cancel ascent. Use the scale bar for distance. Answer in minutes; an answer within 10 minutes of the true value is accepted. Give one number, for example 95.
references: USGS 7.5-minute topographic quadrangle maps (1:24 000, brown contours, bold index contours)

question: This is a topographic map. The contour interval is 20 meters, index contours (heavy lines) are every 100 meters, and elevations are in meters. A ranger must choose one campsite from the magenta points C1, C2, C3 and C4. The site must meet all three rules: (1) it is below 500 m; (2) it is within 300 m of a stream (blue line), measured with the scale bar; (3) it is on gentle ground, where neighbouring contour lines are at least 100 m apart. Exactly one site meets all three rules. Which one? Answer with the site name, for example C2.

checks.margins: elevation 30 m from the limit, stream <=220 m or >=400 m, spacing >=143 m or <=67 m

references: USGS 7.5-minute topographic quadrangle maps (1:24 000, brown contours, bold index contours)
